solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food communications that are unwanted

blocks.note: first meaning: the tinned luncheon meat
second meaning: junk email sent in bulk

explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as if food could be unwanted messages; they are separate senses of one brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinned meat brand gave its name to unsolicited bulk email, after a famous Monty Python sketch.

clue.text: Creep tremulously round female with a few words to start with?

definitions.text: a few words to start with?

indicators.note: something done tremulously is shaky and unsteady, so the letters are shaken out of order
round means surrounding, so the rearranged word goes around the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sidles nervously around a woman, with a little speech prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: CREEP becomes PRECE, with F and A placed inside it. The question mark flags a cryptic-ish definition of an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the brief introductory text at the front of a book, words that come first.

clue.text: Mum has boy who may belong to secret society

definitions.text: who may belong to secret society

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A mother's son might be part of a clandestine group.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons, members of a famously secretive fraternity, are called masons.

clue.text: What operator of cannon will do as a lively person

definitions.text: What operator of cannon will do

blocks.clueFragment: What operator of cannon will do
blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: a gunner will shoot a cannonball
second meaning: an energetic, spirited person

explanation.surface: A gunner described as a lively sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the first meaning: what a gunner does is discharge a round shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle of energy is called a fireball, an idiom drawn from a blazing projectile.

clue.text: Tedious job in the Smoke

blocks.note: first meaning: a chore, something wearisome
second meaning: British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Drudgery in London, which is nicknamed the Smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is a British nickname for London, so the surface suggests a dull job in the capital; here Smoke simply means a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a fag is both a cigarette and a wearisome task.

clue.text: Anger with ship at sea — fresh design results

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fury aboard a vessel leads to a new plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Reshaping is forming something anew, so it amounts to giving it a new design.

clue.text: Foolish talk — see bishop foam

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lather is soapy froth

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken: look at the bishop frothing at the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Blather is long-winded nonsensical chatter, a synonym for drivel.

clue.text: Reveal learner joining college

indicators.note: joining means attaching to, so one piece is placed straight before the next

blocks.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
Eton College is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A student enrols at a college and spills a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for disclosing something, often a secret.

clue.text: Communications taking a long time to get to army room?

blocks.note: a mess is where soldiers eat together
taking ages means taking a long time

explanation.surface: Letters take forever to reach the soldiers' quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a long time' comes first in the clue but its piece goes second; 'to get to' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are communications sent from one person to another, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Some start showing skills

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the answer is only part of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Some people begin to display their talents.
explanation.definitionFit: Arts are skills or crafts, as in the arts of persuasion or the martial arts.

clue.text: One in vehicle is conceited

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The person in the car is full of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain describes someone with an excessively high opinion of their own looks or worth.

clue.text: Be in pain, landing ashore

blocks.note: taken as written
aching means hurting, in pain

explanation.surface: Someone is hurting as they come ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaching a boat means running it up onto the shore, so it is landed.

clue.text: Wicked man undermining pub, West Indian

indicators.note: undermining literally means going beneath, so in a down clue those pieces sit below the other

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
bad means wicked
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A villain wrecks a pub in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, undermining puts the wicked man beneath the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Barbadian is someone from Barbados, an island of the West Indies.

clue.text: Hesitation after beloved becomes more expensive

indicators.note: after means following, so the first-named piece comes second in the answer

blocks.note: a dear is a loved one
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A lover's hesitation drives up the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear can mean costly, so its comparative means costing more.

clue.text: Disapproval concerning strength of spirit

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
proof is the measure of an alcoholic spirit's strength

explanation.surface: Censure about how strong someone's courage or liquor is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strength of spirit' reads as courage but means the alcohol rating of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, an expression of criticism or disapproval.

clue.text: Tragic king's about to go to India or some other country

indicators.note: about in the sense of turned around, so the king's name with its possessive is read backwards
going to a place means arriving at it, so one piece is attached to the other

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: A tragic king is heading off to India or another land.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAR'S is turned to SRAEL and attached to I. 'Some other country' is fair because India itself has just been used.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East, so it is an instance of a country other than India.

clue.text: Eastern scenes, weird in basic quality

indicators.note: something weird is strange and distorted, so these letters are put in an odd new order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange oriental views capture the fundamental character of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic nature of a thing, its fundamental character.

clue.text: Friends knocked over by explosive sound immediately

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: pals are friends
a bang is the sound of an explosion

explanation.surface: Mates are bowled over by a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang is an informal adverb meaning suddenly, at once or directly.

clue.text: Girl given ring? It's ropy!

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A girl gets an engagement ring, which turns out to be shoddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropy' is British slang for poor quality, but here it means made of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope used by cowboys, so it is quite literally made of rope.

clue.text: Swimmer enveloped in surf is happy

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside, so the answer lies within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters are wrapped across the three words

explanation.surface: A swimmer engulfed by waves is having a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is a creature that swims, so 'swimmer' describes it by what it does.

clue.text: Feature a church in newspaper

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so those pieces sit within the newspaper's letters

blocks.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a feature article about a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspaper wants to be the paper's subject; it simply supplies the outer letters, the British Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one aspect or characteristic of something, a synonym of feature.

clue.text: City is huge, look!

blocks.note: OS is short for outsize, as in clothing
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how big a city is.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, an example of a city.

clue.text: Home with no money is guiltless

blocks.note: being in means being at home
no cent: not a single coin

explanation.surface: Being penniless at home proves you did nothing wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent and guiltless are synonyms for not having committed the offence.

clue.text: Fellow turning up gets gesture of acceptance

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means flipping upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man arrives and receives a sign of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head signals agreement or assent.

clue.text: Prisoner punished and locked up

blocks.note: con is short for convict
being fined is a form of punishment

explanation.surface: A convict is punished and imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined means being shut in or imprisoned, a synonym.

clue.text: Come down — listen to group of players

indicators.note: listening means hearing rather than reading, so the answer is a word with the same sound

blocks.note: a team is a group of players, and it is said identically

explanation.surface: An instruction to go downstairs and hear the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down' is meant in the sense of rain falling heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: When rain teems it pours down, so it comes down in torrents.
